heading: Heap = Auto-sorted Min/Max
body:
A **heap** keeps the smallest (or largest) value at the root, always. Push/pop in **O(log n)** via bubble up/down.

**Top-K trick**: Use a size-K min-heap to find K largest elements in O(n log k) — evict the root when a bigger element arrives.

heading: Max-Heap? Negate the values
body:
Python's `heapq` only gives min-heaps. For a max-heap:

```python
heapq.heappush(max_heap, -value)
max_val = -heapq.heappop(max_heap)
```

Negating flips the ordering — smallest negated = largest original.

label: Top-K Largest · Python

q: You need the 5 largest elements from a stream of 1 million numbers. What's the most efficient approach?
options: Maintain a max-heap of all elements, pop 5 times at the end
Maintain a min-heap of size 5, replacing root when larger elements arrive
Sort the array and take the last 5 elements
Use a min-heap of all elements, pop until 5 remain
explain: Size-5 min-heap gives O(n log 5) ≈ O(n) time and O(1) space. The root is the 5th largest—evict it when a larger element arrives.
